purpose: BROWNFIELD EXAMPLE. The spec extracted from code/legacy-cart/cart.js — code that already existed, with a threshold nobody documented, a rejection nobody tested, and one line that turned out to be dead. Shows the three things only brownfield can do: declare a substitution boundary, account for every decision site in the implementation, and measure fidelity against the original instead of asserting it.

excluded.reason: Totals here count quantities; money is the billing area's.
Nothing in this code reserves stock; adding an item does not hold it.

boundary.persistence_contract: The store's cart shape IS the contract — existing carts must remain readable. A replacement may change how it talks to the store, not what a stored cart looks like.
free: how items are looked up (find vs index)
error class names, as long as the call still throws

entities.name: Cart
entities.description: CLOSED, read off the code: `status` is only ever compared to "checked_out" and only ever assigned it. Anything else a regenerated implementation invents (Abandoned, Locked) would be new behavior nobody specified.

externals.name: PaymentGateway
externals.description: Charged at checkout. The code's try/catch says more about it than any document did.

outcomes.name: DECLINED
outcomes.description: Explicitly refused; the cart stays open.

outcomes.name: UNAVAILABLE
outcomes.description: Threw — timeout or transport. The charge may or may not have landed.

assumptions.statement: A charge that throws did not take the money, so retrying is safe.
assumptions.rationale: The code retries on UNAVAILABLE with no idempotency key, so a landed-but-unacknowledged charge would double-charge. Carried as risk because it is what the existing system already does — extracting the spec did not create this exposure, it revealed it. Tracked in Q-002.
assumptions.discharged_by: Nothing today. A gateway idempotency key would discharge it.

requirements.description: While the cart is Open, when a shopper adds a SKU already in the cart, the system shall increase that line's quantity.

meaning.text: Adding something already in the basket makes that line bigger rather than adding a second line for the same product.
meaning.author: agent

ears.trigger: a shopper adds a SKU already present
ears.response: increase that line's quantity by the amount added

requirements.description: While the cart is Open and holds fewer than MAX_ITEMS lines, when a shopper adds a new SKU, the system shall append a line for it.

meaning.text: A product not yet in the basket gets its own line, as long as the basket is still open and has not already reached MAX_ITEMS lines.
meaning.author: agent

ears.state: the Cart is Open and holds fewer than MAX_ITEMS lines
ears.trigger: a shopper adds a new SKU
ears.response: append a line for that SKU

requirements.description: If a shopper adds an item to a CheckedOut cart, then the system shall refuse the call and change nothing.

meaning.text: Once a basket has been checked out it is finished: further attempts to add to it are refused and the basket's contents stay exactly as they were at checkout.
meaning.author: agent

ears.response: refuse the call and leave the cart untouched

witness.justification: A refusal has no reachable state to witness. INV-001 carries the model-side proof.

requirements.description: If the payment gateway is unavailable during checkout, then the system shall leave the cart Open and report that a retry is possible.

meaning.text: If the payment provider fails during checkout, the basket stays open and the shopper is told the checkout did not go through — nothing is half-completed.
meaning.author: agent

ears.trigger: the payment gateway throws during checkout
ears.response: leave the Cart Open and return ok:false with reason 'unavailable'

error_outcomes.effect: NO_CHANGE — the cart stays Open; reason 'declined'
NO_CHANGE — the cart stays Open; reason 'unavailable'; caller retries
error_outcomes.note: Retry safety rests on ASM-001, which is carried as a known risk.

invariants.description: A CheckedOut cart's items never change.
A cart never holds more than MAX_ITEMS distinct lines.

constraints.name: MAX_ITEMS
constraints.description: Maximum distinct lines in a cart. Read off the code — no document mentioned it.

examples.title: Adding a SKU twice merges the lines

extraction_triage.reason: The cart-full rejection is real behavior with no requirement: REQ-002 says what happens BELOW the limit and nothing says what happens at it. Exactly the kind of branch a regenerated implementation would omit.
extraction_triage.question: Q-001

extraction_triage.reason: Returns the updated cart the caller already holds; the observable change is the stored cart, covered by REQ-001/REQ-002.
Checkout of an empty cart throws. No requirement mentions it, and the empty-cart case is not in any journey.
extraction_triage.question: Q-003

extraction_triage.reason: Same site: the threshold itself is unspecified. Is an empty checkout an error, or a no-op returning ok:true?
extraction_triage.question: Q-003

extraction_triage.reason: The empty-cart rejection, unspecified. Note it THROWS while the other two failure paths RETURN ok:false — an inconsistency the extraction surfaced.
extraction_triage.question: Q-003

extraction_triage.reason: store.get always returns a cart today; the guard is a belt against a store contract that has never been violated.
Unreachable given the store's current contract. A finding about the CODE: either delete it, or make the store contract explicit enough that the branch is justified.
clear() has no requirement at all — the whole operation was extracted as code with no spec behind it.
extraction_triage.question: Q-004

extraction_triage.reason: total() sums quantities as a stand-in for an amount; anything money-shaped belongs to billing.

open_questions.question: What should adding an item to a full cart do — throw as today, or return a result the UI can render? The code throws, which no requirement describes.
Retry after a thrown charge assumes the money did not move (ASM-001). Should checkout send an idempotency key before we rely on that?
Checkout of an empty cart THROWS while declined and unavailable RETURN ok:false. Is the inconsistency intentional?
clear() is implemented and unspecified. Is it product behavior, or a leftover from an admin tool?

states.name: CheckedOut
states.description: Frozen; INV-001 keeps its items fixed.
